title: Inspiratory Flow Rate versus Auto-PEEP
subtitle: Assess how inspiratory flow rate changes affect duty cycle timing, auto-PEEP, and airway pressures during volume control

patient.summary: Intubated patient with severe status asthmaticus receiving volume-controlled ventilation.

prediction.question: When inspiratory flow is increased from 30 to 75 L/min at a fixed tidal volume of 500 mL and rate of 18 breaths/min, how will auto-PEEP, peak airway pressure (Ppeak), and plateau pressure (Pplat) change?

whatToLookAtHint: Compare the inspiratory time, expiratory time, peak airway pressure, and end-expiratory alveolar pressure across flow settings.

reflection.question: Why does increasing inspiratory flow from 30 to 75 L/min reduce auto-PEEP in severe airflow obstruction, even though peak airway pressure increases?

options.text: Higher inspiratory flow delivers the set tidal volume faster, shortening Ti and lengthening available expiratory time (Te) for lung emptying.
Higher inspiratory flow generates positive airway vibration that dilates obstructed bronchi.
High flow rates reduce alveolar dead space, lowering CO2 and ventilatory drive.
The ventilator switches from square to decelerating flow pattern automatically at 75 L/min.

reflection.explanation: In volume control with a square flow pattern, Ti = VT / Flow. At 30 L/min (0.5 L/s), delivering 500 mL requires 1.0 s, leaving only 2.33 s for expiration at RR 18. Increasing flow to 75 L/min (1.25 L/s) cuts Ti to 0.4 s, expanding expiratory time to 2.93 s (+0.60 s). This additional time allows more trapped air to escape, decreasing trapped volume, auto-PEEP, and end-inspiratory plateau pressure. Peak pressure rises solely because resistive pressure drop (Flow × R_insp) increases during inspiration.

evidence.claim: Increasing inspiratory flow rate shortens inspiratory time, extending expiratory time and reducing dynamic hyperinflation and intrinsic PEEP at the cost of higher peak inspiratory pressure.
evidence.source: Marini JJ. Dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP: lessons learned over 30 years. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2011;184(7):756-762.

evidence.claim: Adjusting flow rate and duty cycle optimizes expiratory time in obstructive disease.
evidence.source: Tobin MJ. Advances in mechanical ventilation. N Engl J Med. 2001;344(26):1986-1996.
